web.title: Bangladesh, Malaysia set to begin FTA talks today | The Business Standard
web.description: Bangladesh and Malaysia are set to formally begin negotiations on a free trade agreement (FTA) today (27 October), focusing on draft texts, market access, product lists and a timeline for concluding the deal, as both countries seek to expand bilateral trade and reduce existing trade barriers. The talks will launch at 10am at Pan Pacific Sonargaon Hotel in Dhaka, with Commerce Secretary Sharf Uddin Ahmed Choudhury inaugurating the event. The two countries have already exchanged preliminary draft agreements which will be discussed following the opening session, officials of the commerce ministry said.

web.title: Bangladesh-Malaysia Free Trade Talks Open in Dhaka, Target to Finalise Deal by 2027 â Barlekha Today
web.description: Formal talks on a free trade agreement (FTA) to increase bilateral trade and investment between Bangladesh and Malaysia have begun. Representatives of the two countries opened the first round of talks in Dhaka with the target of finalising the agreement by 2027. Commerce Secretary Sharaf Uddin Ahmad Chowdhury inaugurated the first round at the Pan Pacific Sonargaon Hotel in the capital on Tuesday (27 October). At the inaugural session, representatives of the two countries signed Terms of Reference (TOR) to set the outline and scope of the negotiations. The first round will continue until 29 October. Over the three days, the two sides will discuss ways to protect each other's interests on issues including trade in goods and services, rules of origin and customs procedures.

web.title: Dhaka to host trade talks with Malaysia from Oct 27 | The Daily Star
web.description: # Dhaka to host trade talks with Malaysia from Oct 27 Published : 25 October 2026 Updated : 25 October 2026, 23:58 Refayet Ullah Mirdha Bangladesh will begin the first round of negotiations for signing a free trade agreement with Malaysia on October 27, as a delegation from the Southeast Asian nation has already arrived in Dhaka. A 30-member Malaysian team has arrived to start talks with Bangladesh, Commerce Ministry Public Relations Officer Kamal Hossain told The Daily Star. Bangladesh has been negotiating with eight to 10 countries, including Malaysia, to sign trade deals to retain preferential market access after the country's graduation from the least developed country (LDC) category. If not deferred, Bangladesh's LDC graduation is scheduled to take place on November 24 this year. The country has already signed an Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) with Japan in February and a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) with South Korea to secure duty-free market access in the post-LDC era. However, neither the EPA nor the CEPA has come into force yet, as ratification by the respective countries' parliaments is required.
